output.title: I built a habit tracker where missing a day doesn't kill your streak
output.body:
I've deleted more habit apps than I care to admit — usually the day after I missed a workout and watched my 14-day streak vanish. The app didn't fail me; the mechanic did. So I built Streakly to fix that one thing.

The core idea: if you miss a day, you can repair it by doubling up somewhere else in the same week. Your streak survives. The chain stays intact. You don't spiral.

Instead of tracking unbroken daily chains, Streakly scores you against weekly targets — which is actually closer to how behavior-change research says habits form. Miss Monday, nail Tuesday and Wednesday, you're still on track.

It's iOS only right now, private by default (everything stays on-device, no account required, no social feed), and free during beta.

Honest limitations: no Android version yet, retention numbers are self-reported from a single TestFlight cohort (41% of ~800 people still tracking at day 30), and the App Store listing is still in review. It's early.

I'm the builder. I'd genuinely love to hear from people who've quit habit apps before — did the streak mechanic kill it for you, or was it something else? And if you try it, I want to know what breaks.
